subject: Post-call: economic case & pilot sizing for FinLogic AI
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@finlogic.ai>, procurement@finlogic.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 5 Apr 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: economic case & pilot sizing for FinLogic AI

Hi Amit — thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. I captured the cost levers we discussed and a rough pilot sizing so your procurement team can see the economics early.

Summary of pain & goals (from our call)
- Primary pain: inference cost at scale for real-time document parsing (latency target <= 350ms p95). Current invoices show unpredictable token spikes during batch ingest.
- Business goals: reduce per-interaction cost by >=25% while preserving current latency and model quality; pilot to validate predicted unit economics before committing to reserved capacity.

Key assumptions we used for the preliminary model
- Baseline model: transformer-large equivalent (~1.3B dense) running with 8k context for parsing; average request = 220 input tokens + 160 output tokens = 380 tokens/request.
- Monthly request volume (your estimate): 1.2M requests/month.
- Current blended cost (your hosted provider): $0.00045/token (you mentioned range $0.0004–0.0005).

Redwood economic levers & expected impact (pilot-level)
- Batching: continuous batching projected to reduce GPU token compute by ~18–28% depending on traffic shape. For FinLogic's 60% daytime burst profile we modeled ~22% savings.
- KV/prefix caching: for repeated template documents we estimate 10–15% fewer upstream tokens (saves both cost and latency on warm hits).
- Quantization & model variant routing: using an 8-bit quantized variant for lower-criticality routes can save ~12–20% on inference cost per token with minimal quality impact; critical routes stick to full-float.
- Routing by SLA: route low-priority background jobs to cheaper spot pools — ~8% additional savings overall.

Preliminary pilot TCO (conservative estimate)
- Pilot scope: 4-week pilot ingesting 250k requests/week, mirror production routing for a single workspace.
- Infra: 2 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs for steady-state, with autoscaling to 3 for peak bursts.
- Estimated cost (Redwood hosted pilot, token compute + infra + network): ~$9.2k for the 4-week pilot (detailed line items attached in redwood_cost_model_v2.xlsx).
- Extrapolated steady-state monthly run-rate (if pilot savings realized): ~30% lower than your current spend = projected monthly savings of ~$19k on your stated volumes.

Risks & unknowns we flagged
- If average output length increases by >40% the per-request economics degrade materially (we called this out in the model as sensitivity).
- Certain enterprise security requirements (audit retention, custom KMS) add up-front setup costs; we can scope these separately.

Attachments included: redwood_cost_model_v2.xlsx (line-item TCO + sensitivity tabs), finlogic_pilot_summary.pdf (one-page pilot scope and success criteria).

Proposed next steps
1) Rafael to share the two attachments (this email).
2) FinLogic to confirm a preferred pilot start window (your suggested week of Apr 20).
3) Procurement to review the line-item sheet; if acceptable we’ll issue a pilot SOW and a short MoU.
4) Technical kickoff (30–45m) with your infra/ML infra leads to finalize traffic mirroring approach.

Can you confirm procurement's preferred contact and whether the week of Apr 20 still works? If you want tighter numbers I can run the model again with your monthly token distribution by hour (one CSV).

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 6 Apr 2026 09:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: economic case & pilot sizing for FinLogic AI

Rafael — thanks for the thorough recap. A few quick clarifications from our side:

1) Budget constraints: our procurement cap for Q2 pilots is $12k unless we escalate to budget committee. The $9.2k number looks within range, but procurement will need the line-items split by infra vs recurring token spend.
2) Volume confirmation: the 1.2M/month figure is accurate for current customers, but we have a staged ramp: 400k in May, 800k in June, then 1.2M by July. Can the model show staged-month projection?
3) Latency SLA: the p95 <= 350ms is a hard requirement for our chat-parsing pipeline. Please highlight any fallback behavior that could increase p95 during autoscale events.

Request: can you provide a single-page TCO (one-pager) that shows: baseline spend, Redwood pilot cost, projected monthly savings at 100% and 70% realization, and a quick sensitivity to +40% output tokens? Procurement wants that one-pager for the committee call on Wednesday.

If you can get that one-pager and a staged 3-month projection by EOD Tuesday PST, procurement will try to approve without escalation. Also loop in any legal procurement emails if you have an MoU template.

Appreciate it — Amit
Amit Shah
Head of Platform
FinLogic AI
amit.shah@finlogic.ai | +1 (212) 555-0104

On the SLA question: Monica, Rafael — please call out failover behavior and expected p95 variance in the one-pager.

Thanks Amit — will do. Attaching: a one-page economic-summary (finlogic_pilot_summary.pdf) and the updated redwood_cost_model_v2.xlsx with a staged-month tab and an SLA sensitivity row. High-level answers inline below and in the one-pager: 

- Q2 Budget: pilot total ~$9.2k (infra + compute). I split infra vs token spend in tab "line_items" and added a staged projection for May/June/July in "staged_projection".
- Staged ramp: the spreadsheet now shows per-month run-rates and expected monthly savings at 100% and 70% realization. At 70% realization projected monthly savings in July = ~$13.3k.
- SLA behavior: our failover policy keeps a small pool of warm instances in each region for <1s cold-starts; during autoscale events p95 increases by ~40–80ms in our tests (documented in "sla_notes" sheet). If you require hard p95 guarantees we can size the pool or configure pre-warmed capacity (adds ~$1.6k/month to steady-state cost).

Next steps (updated)
- Rafael to send updated one-pager & workbook (attached).
- Procurement to review the line_items tab and confirm whether they can approve $9.2k pilot under decentralized budget. If not, indicate required approvals.
- If procurement signs off, we’ll send a one-page MoU and schedule technical kickoff for Apr 22.

I’m also adding a HubSpot deal link for your reference and a short MoU template if procurement wants to review terms quickly: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/FIN-2026-042 and https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/ABC123
